lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: For hundreds of years, if you made a mistake in pencil... you fixed it with bread.
lines.caption: You fixed it with *BREAD.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Bread crumbs. Rolled into a little ball, they lifted the pencil right off the page.
lines.caption: Bread *crumbs.*

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: So every desk had... a little sandwich on it?
lines.caption: Every desk had a *sandwich?*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Then, in seventeen seventy, a scientist named Joseph Priestley wrote down something odd.
lines.caption: Then came *1770.*

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: A stretchy tree gum... that wiped pencil marks off paper. Better than bread.
lines.caption: A stretchy *tree gum.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: An instrument maker, Edward Nairne, sold little cubes of it. He claimed he grabbed it by accident, instead of his bread crumbs.
lines.caption: Grabbed by *accident?*

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: And this new stuff needed a name...
lines.caption: It needed a *name.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: So they named it after what it did. It rubbed things out.
lines.caption: It *RUBBED* things out.

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Wait... rubber is called rubber... because it erased pencil?
lines.caption: *RUBBER* = it rubs out?!

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Car tires. Rubber bands. Rubber ducks. All named after... fixing mistakes.
lines.caption: Named after *fixing mistakes.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Two sources, Kip. Bread not included.
lines.caption: Two sources. *Bread not included.*
